extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), patent applicants, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to file a reissue application under 35 U.S.C. §251 to correct errors in an issued patent, including statutory requirements, timing limits, procedural steps, and strategic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a patent reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application is filed to correct an error in the patent, where, as a result of the error, the patent is deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to correct substantive errors that affect validity or operability of the patent; the procedure replaces the original patent with a reexamined version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of the error (applicant's error in prosecution/preparation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The error must arise out of an error in conduct made in the preparation and/or prosecution of the application that became the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue addresses mistakes attributable to the applicant (not PTO errors); this limits eligibility for reissue relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for reissue (35 U.S.C. §251) — grounds required
rubrics_metrics.description: The error must cause the patent to be 'deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid, by reason of: (1) a defective specification or drawing, OR (2) by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than he had a right to claim in the patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue is available only where the error fits within these statutory categories (defective disclosure or incorrect scope of claim rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are too narrow or too broad
rubrics_metrics.description: One common reason to file reissue is that the claims in the issued patent are too narrow or too broad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadening reissues are time-limited (see two-year window); narrowing reissues can be used to correct overbroad claims at any time during the patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure contains inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue may be filed when the specification or drawings contain inaccuracies that render the patent defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive errors in disclosure (not merely typographical) that affect the patent's validity or scope are appropriate subjects for reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim or incorrectly claimed foreign priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to claim, or incorrectly claiming, foreign priority in the issued patent is a common reason for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reissue to correct priority/priority-chain errors that affect entitlement dates or claim scope when attributable to applicant error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to refer to or incorrectly referred to prior co-pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in referring to prior co-pending applications can justify reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correcting improper or omitted cross-references that affect disclosure or entitlement may be remedied by reissue if due to applicant error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue can be used to correct inventorship when the inventorship stated in the patent is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship corrections that arise from applicant preparation/prosecution errors may be addressed in reissue; ensure compliance with applicable oath/declaration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive drawing or specification error
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive errors in drawings or specification are a basis for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-minor errors that affect the meaning or scope of the disclosure are appropriate; typographical/minor errors may instead be handled by a certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to adequately claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. §120
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to adequately claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 is a listed common reason for filing reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue can address mistakes in benefit/priority claims that were the result of applicant error in prosecution or application preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of problem with patent oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems with the patent oath or declaration may be corrected via reissue when attributable to applicant error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath/declaration corrections may have special procedural requirements; assess whether reissue is the proper vehicle versus other corrective mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: Certificate of Correction vs Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate of Correction fixes non-substantive errors (typos, minor); Reissue is for substantive errors. Certificates do not change scope and are low cost; reissue can change scope and requires full re-examination and is more expensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certificate of correction for PTO or applicant clerical errors that do not affect scope or validity; use reissue for substantive corrections that may alter claim scope or validity and require new examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope changes allowed in reissue (versus certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue allows scope changes (broadening or narrowing); Certificate of Correction does not allow scope changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reissue may change claim scope, it triggers full re-examination and strategic/legal consequences (e.g., intervening rights, recapture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor responsible for mistake: applicant vs USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of Correction may address mistakes by the USPTO or applicant; reissue is for mistakes by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the error originated with the PTO or the applicant to choose the correct corrective procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: New examination requirement for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applications are subject to full re-examination; all rejections may be re-applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reissue subjects the entire patent to reexamination; all claims (not just amended ones) can be reexamined and rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender requirement (original patent must be surrendered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must surrender the original patent — receiving a 'do-over' with full re-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing reissue means giving up the original patent; weigh this 'surrender' because the reissued patent replaces the original (but retains the original expiration date if granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-year window for broadening reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadening reissue application must be applied for within 2 years from the grant of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking broader claims, the two-year limit is jurisdictional; missing it prevents filing a broadening reissue (narrowing reissue remains available thereafter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for narrowing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrowing reissue can occur at any time during the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no two-year limitation for narrowing reissues; they can be filed throughout the patent term to correct overbroad claims or other narrowing corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture rule (Doctrine of Recapture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter surrendered during prosecution cannot be recovered in reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that intentionally surrendered subject matter during original prosecution are barred from being recaptured via reissue; analyze prosecution history carefully before attempting to recapture surrendered subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights limiting remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants who used the broadened scope before reissue may have intervening rights that limit the patentee's remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When broadening claims via reissue, consider that parties who practiced the claimed invention between original grant and reissue may obtain limiting rights that reduce available relief for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue procedural steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical process: (1) Submit reissue application (with all changes shown); (2) Surrender original patent; (3) Patent re-examined fully (all rejections may be re-applied); (4) New patent issued (with same expiration date as original).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural requirements carefully; explicitly show changes in the reissue application and be prepared for full examination and possible rejections across all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic considerations and risks of filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue creates risk that other claims will be invalidated; all claims, not just amended ones, are subject to re-examination; public access to file makes reissue strategy visible to competitors; often used to expand claim scope to capture infringers not previously covered; consider if continuation application or reexamination is a better alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance potential benefits of correcting or broadening claims against risks: full re-exam, exposure of strategy, possible loss of claim coverage, intervening rights, and expense. Evaluate alternatives (continuation, ex parte reexamination, etc.) before filing.
